correctness.rationale: Direct multiplication gives commutation exactly when the determinant of \(\rho(A)=(a-c,b)\) and \(\rho(B)\) vanishes. Each nonzero \(\rho\)-fiber is a clique, so the problem reduces to the largest set of nonzero vectors with pairwise nonzero determinants. Every nonzero vector is a scalar multiple of a unimodular vector after Chinese-remainder decomposition; hence each chosen vector can be assigned a projective line, and two determinant-independent vectors cannot share one. Conversely, unimodular generators of distinct projective points have nonzero determinant, since a basis change sends one to \((1,0)\). Thus the maximum is \(|\mathbb P^1(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)|\), whose standard unimodular-vector count is Dedekind's psi function. The inspected verifier independently checks projective geometry through n=40, the matrix criterion through n=10, and exact branch-and-bound optima through n=6.

value.rationale: The result gives a uniform exact solution to a concrete published problem, identifies the governing projective geometry, and corrects a proposed formula that fails already at the smallest nonfield example. It is an all-modulus theorem with a natural invariant, not a small numerical counterexample.
residual_risks: Higher triangular dimensions require genuinely different coupled commutator equations.

final_claim: For every \(n\ge2\), the commuting graph on noncentral matrices in \(\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)\) has independence number \(\psi(n)=n\prod_{p\mid n}(1+1/p)=|\mathbb P^1(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)|\). In particular, the proposed value in the 2024 source is false for composite moduli; at \(n=4\) the exact value is \(6\), not \(48\).
limitations: Only 2 by 2 upper triangular matrices over \(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\) are covered.
The theorem determines the independence number but does not classify all maximum independent sets up to automorphism.
